items.item_text: Valid driver’s license or access to reliable transportation for potential off-site meetings and events.

A minimum of 2-3 years of relevant experience in digital fundraising, marketing or constituent engagement. Experience with digital fundraising portfolio management or pipeline development preferred. Fundraising experience in higher education or a nonprofit setting is strongly preferred.
Build and manage a portfolio of leadership annual giving prospects using engagement, giving, demographic, and capacity data.
Develop tailored engagement and solicitation strategies for alumni and current families, recognizing the distinct interests, experiences, and motivations of each constituency.
Develop and execute personalized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies across phone, video, email, text, and other approved digital channels.
Conduct discovery conversations to assess donor interests, philanthropic priorities, giving capacity, and readiness for leadership annual giving or major gift engagement.
Solicit leadership annual gifts and support donor retention, renewal, upgrade, and reactivation efforts through strategic relationship management.
Develop individualized engagement and solicitation strategies in partnership with Leadership Annual Giving colleagues and Advancement partners.
Maintain accurate and timely documentation of constituent interactions, solicitations, gifts, and portfolio activity within the Advancement CRM.
Participate in regular portfolio reviews and facilitate appropriate referrals to Leadership Annual Giving and Major Gifts officers.
Serve as the primary Leadership Annual and Reunion Giving liaison for the 10th and 15th Reunion Committees.
Partner with reunion volunteers to develop and execute fundraising strategies that increase participation, encourage leadership annual giving, and advance reunion campaign goals.
Provide volunteers with fundraising guidance, prospect information, outreach strategies, and stewardship support.
Help recruit, orient, engage, and steward class volunteers to strengthen long-term alumni involvement and philanthropic participation.

Partner with Leadership Annual Giving officers, Advancement Services, Research and Prospect Development, Alumni and Family Engagement, and Advancement Communications on donor strategy, prospect identification, outreach, and engagement initiatives.
Support Giving Day, reunion campaigns, and other annual giving initiatives that include leadership-level donor engagement, volunteer fundraising, matching gifts, and digital outreach.
Help establish and refine portfolio management practices, digital engagement strategies, reporting standards, and performance benchmarks for Pomona's Digital Gift Officer program.
Analyze donor engagement and fundraising performance data to evaluate outcomes and improve future strategies.
Stay informed of emerging trends in digital fundraising and donor engagement and recommend new approaches that support annual giving goals.
Growth in leadership-level ($1,500+) donor acquisition, renewals, upgrades, reactivation, and revenue resulting from digital outreach and relationship-building strategies.
Development and active management of a qualified digital portfolio of leadership annual giving prospects, with appropriate documentation, staging, and movement within the Advancement CRM.
Increased conversion of qualified prospects into the Leadership Annual and Major Gift pipelines.
Consistent execution of high-quality digital outreach and substantive donor conversations that advance prospects through the cultivation and solicitation cycle.

Increased participation and leadership-level giving within assigned reunion classes through effective partnership with reunion volunteers and fundraising committees, including the 10th- and 15th-Reunion Committees.
Strong digital campaign performance across core metrics (open rates, conversion, renewal, reactivation).
